news.title: Radio presenters were 1966 World Cup heroes too
news.lede: Andrew Keeley will never forget Brian Moore and Alan Clarke’s commentary on BBC radio. Garry Richardson (England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars, 30 July) appears to make the assumption that everyone watched the 1966 World Cup final on television with Kenneth Wolstenholme’s iconic commentary. As a football-mad 10-year-old, I had the misfortune on the day of the final to be on our family summer holiday in the then sleepy village of Goathland, staying in a house with no TV. Hope rose when my dad was invited to watch the final at a neighbour’s who had one of the few TVs in the village and he asked if he could bring his children.

news.title: Explained: Why Is Gianni Infantino Suddenly Fighting for His FIFA Presidency?
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has survived corruption scandals, Super League battles and World Cup controversies. Now, the FIFA president faces perhaps his biggest political challenge yet. England's Football Association is preparing to withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election, joining a growing European revolt after FIFA's controversial proposal to sell minority stakes in a commercial entity managing the World Cup and other tournaments. Why is the Football Association withdrawing support for Gianni Infantino?

news.title: Pochettino to stay as USA coach until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Mauricio Pochettino has signed a contract extension to remain the head coach of the United States national team until the 2030 World Cup, US Soccer announced Monday. The 54-year-old took over in 2024 and led the USA to the last 16 at the recent World Cup, which they co-hosted with Canada and Mexico. "It has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the men's national team program even stronger," said Argentinian Pochettino, whose coaching staff have also agreed new contracts. "The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here...

news.title: Morocco Mourns Pioneering World Cup Referee Jilali Gharib
news.lede: Rabat – The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) announced on Sunday the death of former international referee Jilali Gharib, a pioneering figure in Moroccan football officiating. In a statement published on its official website, the federation extended its condolences to Gharib’s family and paid tribute to his contribution to Moroccan football. FRMF president Fouzi Lekjaa also honored the late referee, describing him as one of the country’s most distinguished officials and recalling his historic achievement as the first Moroccan referee to participate in a FIFA World Cup.

news.title: Infantino addresses the Egyptian Football Association with a special message about the World Cup
news.lede: What the FIFA president said about an Egypt national team legend. FIFA president Gianni Infantino sent an official message to the Egyptian Football Association on Monday. In his telegram, Infantino offered his sincere congratulations to Al Ahly's current football director and wished him continued health, happiness and success on both a personal and professional level, praising his great career as a player and administrator. The message singled out the role played by former Egypt and Al Ahly star Wael Gomaa, with Infantino affirming that his support and cooperation contributed directly to the success of the first World Cup staged under its new 48-team format.

news.title: The general director of the German Football Federation states that the relationship between the German federation and FIFA is impossible to repair, following the scandal involving the investors from the World Cup.
news.lede: Andreas Rettig, the CEO of the German Football Association (DFB), stated that the relationship between the DFB and FIFA is impossible to repair, following the scandal related to investors at the World Cup and other governance issues. In an interview with Stern magazine, Rettig emphasized that there has been an "irreparable loss" of trust. He criticized the decisions made behind closed doors and the dishonest tactics used to attract investors. Rettig mentioned that FIFA President Gianni Infantino has surrounded himself with business people, which is incompatible with the principles of football.
